issues.legal_issue: A certificate authenticating a secondary electronic record is required when the record is tendered as evidence at trial, not when the charge sheet is filed or a discharge application is considered.
material_facts: The prosecution relied on a spy-camera recording as well as other material listed in the charge sheet.
No certificate authenticating the electronic record accompanied the charge sheet.
The case was at the pretrial discharge stage, and the electronic record had not yet been tendered in evidence.
issues.conclusion: The absence of the certificate when the charge sheet was filed did not make the prosecution liable to fail or justify quashing the proceedings at the discharge stage; the certificate would be required when the electronic record was sought to be used as evidence at trial.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 65B(4) of the Evidence Act, the certificate requirement arises when an electronic record is sought to be used as evidence. Anvar P.V. v P.K. Basheer held that the certificate must accompany the electronic record when it is produced in evidence. Union of India v CDR Ravindra V Desai and Sonu alias Amar v State of Haryana establish that failure to produce the certificate may be cured at the stage of marking the record.

rule.if: pretrial_discharge_proceeding and electronic_record_relied_on and certificate_absent_at_charge_sheet and record_not_yet_tendered

predicates.pretrial_discharge_proceeding: The court was considering whether a criminal prosecution should proceed before evidence was tendered at trial.
predicates.electronic_record_relied_on: The prosecution relied on a computer-generated electronic record as part of its case.
predicates.certificate_absent_at_charge_sheet: The prosecution filed its charge sheet without the certificate authenticating the electronic record.
predicates.record_not_yet_tendered: The electronic record had not yet been offered as evidence at trial.

issues.definition: When a prosecution relies on an electronic record but has not yet tendered it at trial, the absence of its certificate at the charge-sheet or discharge stage does not require the prosecution to be stopped.

issues.legal_issue: A limited preliminary inquiry into whether information reveals a cognizable offence may occur before registration of a first information report without constituting commencement of the investigation.
material_facts: The allegation concerned corruption by a public servant.
Before the first information report was registered, the investigating officer gave the complainant a spy camera.
The camera was used to record a meeting for the purpose of assessing whether the information disclosed a cognizable offence.
issues.conclusion: The pre-report activity was a preliminary inquiry to ascertain whether the information revealed a cognizable offence, not the commencement of an investigation, and was consistent with the law governing preliminary inquiries.
issues.legal_principle: P. Sirajuddin v State of Madras recognized the need for a suitable preliminary inquiry into allegations of serious misconduct by a public servant before lodging a first information report. Lalita Kumari v Government of Uttar Pradesh held that a preliminary inquiry may be conducted in specified categories, including corruption cases, for the limited purpose of ascertaining whether the information reveals a cognizable offence. Section 154 of the Code of Criminal Procedure governs registration of information in cognizable cases.

predicates.corruption_allegation_against_public_ser: A person reported an allegation of corruption against a public servant.
predicates.pre_fir_assessment_activity: Before a first information report was registered, an investigating officer arranged activity to assess the reported information.
predicates.activity_limited_to_cognizable_offence_a: The pre-report activity was limited to determining whether the reported information disclosed a cognizable offence.

issues.definition: When a pre-report activity in a corruption matter is limited to assessing whether the reported information discloses a cognizable offence, it is a preliminary inquiry rather than an investigation.

issues.legal_issue: At the discharge stage, the court must assess the prosecution material on its face value for grounds to presume that an offence was committed, rather than conduct a mini trial or assess whether conviction is certain.
material_facts: The respondent sought discharge under Section 239 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
The charge sheet referred to material apart from the spy-camera recording.
The High Court rejected the prosecution's reliance on that other material as unconvincing without assessing it under the discharge-stage standard.
The trial court had dismissed the discharge application.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in quashing the proceedings. The Supreme Court allowed the appeal and maintained the trial court's dismissal of the discharge application.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 239 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the court considers whether the facts emerging from the prosecution material, taken at face value, disclose the ingredients of the offence and whether there is ground for presuming that the accused committed it. The court may consider the probative value of the material but must not decide whether it warrants conviction or conduct a mini trial. State of Tamil Nadu v N Suresh Rajan states this standard.

predicates.discharge_application_proceeding: The court was deciding an application to discharge an accused before trial.
predicates.charge_sheet_contains_prosecution_materi: The prosecution's charge sheet included material on which it relied to support the alleged offence.
predicates.face_value_material_discloses_offence_in: Taken at face value, the prosecution material disclosed the ingredients of the alleged offence.

issues.definition: When a discharge application is before the court and the charge-sheet material, taken at face value, discloses the offence's ingredients, the application should be rejected without deciding whether the material will establish guilt at trial.
